title: Azure provisioning spec
description: Declarative input for web-forge's azure-provision skill: mint a service principal through a portal session, then provision resources unattended. Instances live in the consuming project repo, never in cc-skills.

identity.description: Identity preflight. Checked with assertIdentity() BEFORE anything is created, because a resource minted under the wrong signed-in account is a silent disaster.

tenantDomain.description: The Entra tenant's domain, e.g. contoso.onmicrosoft.com. Used in error messages only.

expectedAccount.description: The account that MUST be signed in, e.g. admin@contoso.ca. Compared against the captured token's upn with any federation prefix stripped (a guest/MSA account arrives as 'live.com#admin@contoso.ca').

id.description: Subscription GUID. Discover it from the portal's Subscriptions blade first — note that `az account list` returning [] proves nothing while the CLI is Conditional-Access blocked.

displayName.description: App registration display name. Must be unique in the tenant: minting refuses if more than one already matches, rather than adding another.

secretDescription.description: Label shown on the client secret in the portal. Defaults to a web-forge marker.

roleDefinitionId.description: Built-in role GUID to assign at subscription scope. Defaults to Contributor (b24988ac-6180-42a0-ab88-20f7382dd24c). Contributor deliberately CANNOT create further role assignments — do not upgrade to Owner without a reason.

vault.description: Where the minted credential is written. All four are required together: a client id without its tenant, or a secret without its client id, is unusable.

clientSecretPath.description: Dot-path for the client secret. Written via `vault set --stdin`; never argv.

tenantIdPath.description: Dot-path for the tenant id, taken from the captured token's `tid` claim.

subscriptionIdPath.description: Optional dot-path for the subscription id, so consumers need only one scope.

name.description: Resource group name, created if absent.

location.description: Azure region, e.g. canadacentral. Pick for data residency, not latency, when PHI/PII is involved.

resources.description: Cognitive Services accounts to provision. Each writes its key AND endpoint together — see the `credentials` requirement.

name.description: Resource name, which also becomes the custom subdomain. This is GLOBALLY unique across all of Azure — a name already used in someone else's subscription will fail, so migrations typically need a suffix.

sku.description: SKU name, e.g. F0 (free, one per kind per subscription) or S0.

credentials.description: Key and endpoint are written TOGETHER and both are required. Rotating a key while an endpoint stayed a hardcoded literal elsewhere produced a production HTTP 401 ('invalid subscription key or wrong API endpoint'); modelling them as one unit makes that class of drift impossible here.

endpointPath.description: Dot-path for the resource endpoint URL.

regionPath.description: Optional dot-path for the region — required by Speech SDKs that take a region rather than an endpoint.

preserveExistingAs.description: Optional prefix. If set, any existing value at each path is copied to `<prefix>_<path>` before being overwritten, so a migration stays reversible.

acceptanceCheck.description: Proves the resource DETECTS, not merely authenticates. A 200 on a trivial call is not evidence the resource works.

kind.description: pii-entities: POST synthetic text, require >= minEntities back. speech-token: require an issueToken 200 with a non-trivial token.

sampleText.description: Synthetic probe text. MUST NOT contain real personal data.

minEntities.description: Minimum entities the probe must return for the check to pass.

teardownBrowser.description: Kill the automation Chrome when minting finishes (default true). Set false to keep the session for a follow-up run.
